claims.title: Zero-field Ising has paid parity-sampling equivalences and precise shortcut obstructions

quoted_fields.interface: Every explicitly labelled finite simple graph, including arbitrary degree, disconnected graphs and isolated vertices; rational heterogeneous beta_e>=1 in binary, complete binary length B, n=|V|, and rational 0<epsilon<=1/2. Target is the unconditional full-joint zero-field Ising spin law proportional to product_e beta_e^[equal endpoint spins]. Gates have bounded fan-in; every execution must have polynomial Boolean work and random bits in n+B+epsilon^-1 and polylogarithmic depth, with fixed computable constants. No uniform activity gap, real arithmetic, conditional oracle, postselection or unpaid rejection is supplied.
quoted_fields.failure: The full uniform heterogeneous all-temperature zero-field finite-bit RNC sampler is not constructed; neither a qualifying lower bound nor an independently justified full-model hardness reduction is supplied. The exact reduction identifies a missing core, not its solution. Gaussian elimination handles uniform cycle-space sampling, not the biased parity-conditioned law. Supplied Chen-Liu-Yin-Zhang fixed interaction/nonzero-field gaps and CRCW costs, Miao uniform tree-uniqueness expected arithmetic work, and fixed-temperature sequential results do not supply the requested core. Their literature descriptions are retained as supplied/producer-reported scopes, not new Capital governing-paper reads or a comprehensive current novelty determination. No original ZIP was visible; no additional attachment, cited paper or held identity was acquired. Displayed model is 5.6 Pro at collection; exact model throughout, hidden helpers and compute are unconfirmed.
